t: This Act may be cited as the “Omnibus Indian Advancement Act”.

fable.w: This section is only a short-title provision naming the Act. The word "Indian" in the title might suggest tribal involvement, but a proper noun alone creates no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government.

opus.w: This is a short-title provision that only gives the Act its name. It creates no process for outside parties to take part in a federal decision. The word "Indian" in the title might suggest tribal consultation, but a name in boilerplate is not a participation mechanism.
opus.b: **Step 1, analysis.** The tempting reading is that "Indian Advancement" points to tribal involvement, and tribes are outside the federal government. That reading fails. This is only a short-title clause. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue, so no outside party takes part in any federal decision.
